traps.text: Our first food pantry was sparked by a fire at the community centre in 1998, and it has opened every Saturday since.
traps.why: The first defect of this class. `parked (?:free )?(?:courtesy of|by)` shipped with no left boundary and matched inside `sparked by`; its only two matches in 44,284 corpus pages were live organization sites of about 3,000 characters that the instrument was reporting unreachable. PARKED_RX carries `\bparked` because of this sentence.

traps.text: Send us a message using the form below. This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Google Privacy Policy and Terms of Service apply.
traps.why: The second defect of this class. The bare word `captcha` matched inside `reCAPTCHA` in the footer sentence every GoDaddy, Wix and Squarespace contact page prints, and left 64 live organization pages unreachable. The wall vocabulary now asks to SOLVE one, so neither form matches this; a bare token added back would move only one of them.

The intended difference, and the reason this test asks for a comment instead of a boundary. `doGTranslate` is GTranslate's own function name and the vendor's marker on pages that carry nothing else; core.py records that `doGTranslate` was dropped from the pattern precisely because `gtranslate` already matched inside it, measured at 0 organizations added over 45,100. A left boundary here would lose that marker.

traps.text: Before you launch, work through our security checklist and confirm every volunteer account has been reviewed.
traps.why: The case the right-hand boundary was added for. A LEFT boundary says nothing about the character behind a match, so `security check` matched inside `security checklist` under both forms and this file recorded that as what the gate did not cover. In 0.2.0 the alternative carries a right boundary and this sentence is read as what it is, a page telling volunteers to work through a list before launch.

traps.text: The centre offers weekend English classes, a legal clinic on Tuesdays, and a food pantry that any resident of the county may use without an appointment.
traps.why: A negative control. An ordinary page of an organization carries none of this vocabulary, and a corpus made only of positives cannot show that.

traps.text: Nuestro centro ofrece clases de inglés, asesoría legal y una despensa de alimentos abierta a cualquier residente del condado.
traps.why: The same negative control in Spanish. Every gate in this family was written in English, and the pages it must not reach are not all in English.

traps.text: The move caused just a momentary gap in the pantry schedule, and Tuesday hours resumed the same week.
traps.why: `just a moment` is the Cloudflare interstitial and it matched inside `momentary`, which is an ordinary word in a sentence about a service that paused for a week. WALL_UNGATED_RX decides on its own at any page length, so this page was reported as a site nobody read.

traps.text: The staff export lists two dormant logins under not authorized_users, and the office reviews that column every quarter.
traps.why: `not authorized` matched inside `not authorized_users`, a column name a person can reasonably write on a page about record keeping. An underscore is a word character, so the right boundary is what refuses it.

traps.text: Immigration law is a domain not founded on guesswork, and our attorneys sit the training every year.
traps.why: `domain not found` matched inside `domain not founded`. `founded`, `founder` and `foundation` are three of the commonest words on a nonprofit page, and this alternative is ungated, so the reach costs a live organization its whole reading.

traps.text: A site not founded by the people who use it is a site nobody visits twice, which is why we ran four listening sessions first.
traps.why: `site not found` inside `site not founded`. The same word and the same ungated pattern as the entry above, on the alternative that carries the shortest wording of the three.

traps.text: A website not founded on what families actually asked for gets rebuilt within the year.
traps.why: `website not found` inside `website not founded`. The third of the three `found` wordings in WALL_UNGATED_RX, held here so a change to one of them cannot quietly leave the others behind.

traps.text: We are doing some workshops on tenant rights this autumn and the first three are already full.
traps.why: `we are doing some work` matched inside `we are doing some workshops`, which is a sentence a community organization writes about its programme. The wording is a maintenance interstitial and this page is the opposite of one.

traps.text: This site is currently privately funded by two family foundations and carries no advertising.
traps.why: `this site is currently private` matched inside `currently privately`. The wording is meant to catch a login wall, and `privately funded` is a statement about money.

traps.text: The requested page about our founder explains how the centre was not founded by a church but by six families.
traps.why: `requested (?:url|resource|page) .{0,60}not found` matched inside `not founded`, reached across the wildcard the alternative carries. A page describing its own history is the page this pattern must never reach.

traps.text: We fixed the 404 errors two volunteers reported on the events calendar last week.
traps.why: `404 ... error` matched inside `404 errors`, which is what a site writes when it has REPAIRED something rather than when it is broken.

traps.text: Every page not founded on a real question from a family gets cut in the next redesign.
traps.why: `page (?:not found|cannot be found)` matched inside `page not founded`. The last of the `found` wordings, in the pattern gated to 300 characters, where a short page of plain prose is exactly what the gate lets through.

The one right boundary that predates 0.2.0, on `smartling-[a-z]{2}` in MT_RX and ROUTE_WIDGET. core.py records that a Smartling install signs itself with a `smartling-<lang>` body class, so the two letters are a language code and have to be the whole of the token; without the boundary any longer class name beginning `smartling-` and two letters is read as an installed translation vendor, which decides a verdict. No claim is made here about how often a class of this shape occurs; the string is what says what the boundary refuses.
